title: Flap Track Fairing Attachment and Drain Provision Rework
abstract: A revised fairing attachment and a positive drain at the flap track fairing, after trapped water and attachment fretting began producing cracked fairing lugs on aircraft in tropical service.

sections.reason: Cracked attachment lugs were found on eight fairings across four operators, all of them based in high rainfall regions and all with more than thirty thousand flight cycles. The fairing traps water at the aft attachment because the drain relies on a hole that the sealant bead closes over during the first repaint, and the trapped water accelerates the fretting that the attachment already suffers from flap cycling. A detached fairing is a release-to-service event and a potential impact on the trailing edge, so the finding was treated as urgent.
sections.description: The aft attachment is changed from a single lug to a twin-lug arrangement with a spherical bearing, so that the fairing can follow the track without loading the lug in bending. The actuator assembly D2750136872416 is refitted with a revised bracket and clevis pins AES390161K8 are used at both lugs. A moulded drain fitting replaces the drilled hole and is set proud of the sealant land so that a repaint cannot close it. Titanium bolts EN621362K1 secure the new bracket. Transmitter 339CE7 on the track and solenoid 984CE in the outboard position are refitted without change. Work is at the left flap area in zone 564 and at the right slat and flap areas in zones 654 and 662, with the flaps at full extension on jacks. Detail is on drawing D27501326743.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 2.8 kg per aircraft over the four fairings. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: a reworked fairing needs the reworked bracket and the two must be embodied as a pair. The fairing lug inspection moves from a detailed visual at every heavy check to a general visual, and the drain check is added to the transit walk-around. Structure repair content for the lug is withdrawn because the new lug is not repairable in situ.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut into production at MSN S01705. Retrofit is available at any C-check with the flaps extended and supported, sixty-four manhours per aircraft. Removed fairings are returned only where a lug crack has been recorded.
